en.headline: Council refers suspected commercial surrogacy case involving mainland influencer to…
en.dek: The Council on Human Reproductive Technology said commercial surrogacy and related advertising are prohibited under the Human Reproductive Technology Ordinance.
body: Hong Kong’s Council on Human Reproductive Technology has referred a case to law enforcement agencies after a mainland Chinese influencer was suspected of offering commercial surrogacy services that involved bringing non-local surrogate mothers to the city.

The influencer, Tan Zubiao, also known as Berlin Sun, had set up a company in Hong Kong and advertised on social media, according to local media reports. He and his husband were recently deported from Taiwan after being fined for offering assisted-reproductive services without proper licensing.

In a reply, the council said commercial surrogacy arrangements and the distribution of related advertisements are prohibited under the Human Reproductive Technology Ordinance. The Department of Health had passed the matter to the council, which sought legal advice before handing the file to enforcement authorities.
Commercial surrogacy remains a criminal offence in Hong Kong regardless of where the arrangement is made.

zh.headline: 人類生殖科技管理局轉介疑涉商業代孕個案予執法部門
zh.dek: 管理局表示，根據《人類生殖科技條例》，商業代母安排及分發有關廣告屬違法。
body: 香港人類生殖科技管理局已將一宗個案轉介執法部門跟進。事件涉及一名內地網紅疑在港設立公司，並在社交媒體宣傳商業代孕服務，聲稱可安排非本地代母來港產子。
該名網紅譚祖彪，網上名為柏林，近日與丈夫在台灣因未獲許可提供輔助生育服務而被罰款並遭遞解出境。本地傳媒報道指他在香港有公司登記。
管理局回覆表示，商業代母安排及分發相關廣告受《人類生殖科技條例》禁止。衛生署已將案件轉介管理局，管理局在尋求法律意見後，已將案件交予執法部門。
在香港，商業代孕屬刑事罪行，不論安排在何處進行。
